subject: Concurrency qualification: streaming targets & Redwood rate limits
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Perez <maria.perez@ariasys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Oct 2028 21:30:00 +0000
Subject: Concurrency qualification: streaming targets & Redwood rate limits

Hi Maria — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Recap of what you asked for
- SLO targets: 95th pct latency for short-turn (<= 64 tokens) conversational responses: <= 250 ms; streaming tail latency (token arrival) target: <= 600 ms under load.
- Throughput: sustained aggregate token-rate target ~ 1.2M tokens/min during peak marketing campaigns; typical baseline ~ 200k tokens/min.
- Concurrency: peak parallel streaming sessions ≈ 180 active sessions, with expected connection reuse across ~60 service nodes. Burst tolerance required to 320 concurrent sessions for ~30s windows.
- Behaviour: each session streams ~80–160 tokens on average; many sessions keep an idle websocket open between bursts.

Immediate asks
1) Can you share a short traffic sample (timestamps + tokens per request) so we can run a pilot traffic replay?
2) Confirm whether sessions are sticky to a region (you mentioned us-west1) and whether you require per-connection client auth (mTLS/API key).
3) Procurement timeline / PO lead (we can start the pilot on a credit basis while the contract closes).

What Redwood can do for pilot
- Pilot capacity: we can reserve a connection pool of 150 concurrent streaming sessions, with automatic burst to 320 for 30s.
- Rate limits: suggest soft token-rate cap 60k tokens/min per tenant during pilot with hard throttles configurable by route.
- Observability: per-connection latency histograms, token-level cost, and tail-drop alerts.
- Rollout: canary in us-west1, followed by regional fan-out if telemetry meets SLOs.

Next steps
- If you can send a traffic sample + preferred pilot window, we’ll produce a trial config and a proposed rate card.

Thanks — I’m looping Marissa here for the rate card and ops handoff.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0194

Attachment: traffic_profile_q4.csv (referenced)

From: Maria Perez <maria.perez@ariasys.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@ariasys.com
Date: Wed, 18 Oct 2028 22:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Concurrency qualification: streaming targets & Redwood rate limits

Jonas — thanks for the write-up, that matches our conversation. A couple clarifications and I attached a small sample: traffic_profile_q4.csv.

Clarifications
- Region: yes, sessions originate to us-west1 only for this application (no multi-region routing initially).
- Auth: we use API keys today; mTLS is on the roadmap but not required for pilot.
- Sticky sessions: some upstream load balancers re-use TCP connections; we will aim for connection affinity but cannot guarantee it.

Numbers from our side (from the attached sample)
- Average concurrent active streams during peak hour: 170–190.
- Connection reuse: roughly 2.6 requests per open TCP connection on average.
- Typical generation length: mean 120 tokens, 95th 340 tokens.

Procurement
- Procurement has been CC’d. We are targeting a Pilot PO by the end of next week if the technical trial looks good.

Please share the pilot config and proposed rate card; we care about how hard throttles interact with streaming (we can’t accept mid-stream truncation on the happy path).

— Maria Perez
Head of Product Integrations | Aria Systems
maria.perez@ariasys.com

Attachment: traffic_profile_q4.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Perez <maria.perez@ariasys.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Oct 2028 09:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Concurrency qualification: streaming targets & Redwood rate limits

Hi Maria — following Jonas’ note I’m attaching a draft rate card and pilot config. High level offer: 

Pilot proposal (config + UX notes)- Reserved connection pool: 150 concurrent streaming sessions (reserved).
- Burst policy: allow up to 320 concurrent streams for up to 60 seconds every 10 minutes (configurable).
- Token throttling: soft limit 60k tokens/min (gentle backpressure), hard cap 120k tokens/min (will start rejecting new requests when exceeded) — for pilot we can lower the hard cap to avoid mid-stream truncation and instead queue/fail new sessions.
- Per-connection limits: recommend a per-connection parallel request cap of 6 to avoid head-of-line issues when many small requests share TCP sockets.
- Observability hooks: RT metrics stream, token latency histograms, connection occupancy dashboard.

Commercial + next steps
- Proposed rate card attached (proposed_rate_card_q3.pdf). For pilot we can do a 30-day credit-backed trial with the above reservation and a discounted overage rate.
- Ops cadence: onboarding call + test window (we usually do a 72-hour replay test), then a 2-week functional pilot.

Notes on streaming safety: we will not mid-stream drop happy-path tokens during the pilot — instead, when hard caps are hit we’ll prefer rejecting new sessions or slowing token emission. If you need guaranteed completion of in-flight streams, we can add a completion-priority queue for confirmed sessions (requires additional reserved capacity).

I’ll set up the pilot config in us-west1 once we get the traffic sample and the preferred trial dates.

— Marissa Cole
Product Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: proposed_rate_card_q3.pdf

From: Maria Perez <maria.perez@ariasys.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@ariasys.com
Date: Thu, 19 Oct 2028 16:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Concurrency qualification: streaming targets & Redwood rate limits

Marissa / Jonas — this is helpful, thanks. We’re signed up for the pilot cadence. A couple quick asks before we kick off: 

1) Can you confirm you will not mid-stream truncate happy-path responses during the pilot? We prefer new-session rejections over truncation.
2) Share SOC2 docs and any network architecture notes for our security team.
3) Procurement will prepare a PO for the pilot credit; procurement@ariasys.com will follow up with a preferred start date (targeting next Monday).

If the pilot demonstrates we can hold the 95th/streaming tail targets at your proposed reservation level we’ll move to a reserved capacity contract.

Thanks — I’ll loop our procurement lead directly for dates.

— Maria Perez
Head of Product Integrations | Aria Systems
maria.perez@ariasys.com
